# simplytest.me

> Launch a temporary Drupal site with any project from drupal.org (a module, theme, distribution, or Drupal core itself) at a chosen version, with optional patches. Sandboxes are free, need no account, and are deleted two hours after launch.

People use it to try a module before installing it, reproduce a bug, or check whether a patch from a drupal.org issue applies and works. Every sandbox has an administrator account: username `admin`, password `admin`.

## Send a launch link

To help someone try a project, build a link and give it to them. The link opens the launch form with the project, version, Drupal core version, install profile, and patches filled in. The person checks them and clicks Launch. Prefer this to launching through the API: the person sees what will be built, and nothing is created until they ask for it.

```
https://simplytest.me/project/{project}/{version}?core={core}&profile={profile}&patch[]={patch_url}
```

- `{project}`: the drupal.org machine name, as in `https://www.drupal.org/project/{project}`. Use `drupal` for Drupal core.
- `{version}`: a release, such as `8.x-1.15` or `2.0.3`, or a dev branch, such as `8.x-1.x` or `2.0.x`. Leave it out (`/project/{project}`) to let the person choose.
- `core`: optional. The Drupal core version: a release (`11.3.2`), a minor (`11.3`), or a major (`11`). A minor or major picks its newest stable release. Without it, or when the project does not support it, the form picks the newest stable release the project supports. Ignored when `{project}` is `drupal`.
- `profile`: optional. `standard` (the default), `minimal`, or `demo_umami`. Ignored for a distribution, which installs with its own profile.
- `patch[]`: optional, and can repeat. The URL of a patch file or merge request diff hosted on `https://www.drupal.org` or `https://git.drupalcode.org`. URL-encode it if it contains `?` or `&`.

Examples:

- https://simplytest.me/project/pathauto/8.x-1.15
- https://simplytest.me/project/pathauto/8.x-1.15?core=10.3&profile=minimal
- https://simplytest.me/project/pathauto/8.x-1.x?patch[]=https://git.drupalcode.org/project/pathauto/-/merge_requests/{id}.diff

A project simplytest.me has not seen before is imported from drupal.org when the link is opened.

## Link to a demo

Demos are ready-made Drupal sites that need no project. Each has a landing page that launches it in one click.

- `GET https://simplytest.me/one-click-demos` lists the demos. Each one's `url` is its landing page.
- `GET https://simplytest.me/site-templates` lists Drupal CMS site templates. The `Demo` entry in each one's `links` is its landing page.

## JSON API

Every endpoint is public and needs no authentication. Send `Accept: application/json`, and `Content-Type: application/json` with a request body. Paths are relative to `https://simplytest.me`.

### Find projects and versions

- `GET /simplytest/projects/autocomplete?string={text}`: projects simplytest.me knows about whose name matches, as `[{"title", "shortname", "type"}]`.
- `POST /simplytest/projects/lookup` with `{"name": "{project}"}`: imports a project from drupal.org that autocomplete does not find yet. Returns 404 when drupal.org has no such project. Limited to 50 lookups an hour per IP address.
- `GET /simplytest/project/{project}/versions`: the project's releases. `list.latest` holds the newest releases, `list.branches` the dev branches, and `list.core` the releases grouped by the Drupal core major version they support. Each release has a `version` and a `core_compatibility` Composer constraint.
- `GET /simplytest/core/compatible/{project}/{version}`: the Drupal core releases that release of the project supports, newest first. Each has a `version`, and `insecure` is `"1"` for a release with a security advisory.

### Launch a sandbox

Launching creates a real sandbox. Only launch when the person asked for a running site, not to answer a question. Each IP address can launch 20 sandboxes an hour.

`POST /launch-project`:

```json
{
  "project": {"shortname": "pathauto", "version": "8.x-1.15", "patches": []},
  "drupalVersion": "11.4.8",
  "installProfile": "standard",
  "manualInstall": false,
  "additionalProjects": [{"shortname": "token", "version": "8.x-1.17"}]
}
```

- `project.version`: a `version` from `/simplytest/project/{project}/versions`.
- `project.patches`: patch URLs, under the same rules as `patch[]` in a launch link.
- `drupalVersion`: a `version` from `/simplytest/core/compatible/{project}/{version}`.
- `installProfile`: `standard`, `minimal`, or `demo_umami`.
- `manualInstall`: `true` leaves the Drupal installer for the person to run.
- `additionalProjects`: optional. Other projects to add to the sandbox. Each must already be known to simplytest.me, so look it up first if autocomplete does not find it.

`POST /one-click-demos/{id}` launches a demo by the `id` from `/one-click-demos`, with no body.

Both answer:

```json
{
  "status": "OK",
  "progress": "https://simplytest.me/tugboat/progress/{instance}/{job}",
  "statusUrl": "https://simplytest.me/tugboat/status/{instance}/{job}",
  "expiresAt": "2026-10-07T22:26:27+00:00"
}
```

Give the person `progress`: it shows the build and signs them in when it finishes. Poll `statusUrl` yourself.

### Check on a sandbox

Request the `statusUrl` every five seconds or so:

```json
{
  "status": "ready",
  "progress": 100,
  "patchFailed": false,
  "url": "https://{preview}.tugboatqa.com",
  "expiresAt": "2026-10-07T22:26:27+00:00",
  "logs": [{"message": "..."}]
}
```

- `status`: `building` (keep polling), `ready` (the site is at `url`), or `failed` (`logs` shows why).
- `patchFailed`: `true` when a patch could not be applied. On a `ready` sandbox, the site is running without that patch, so tell the person.
- `expiresAt`: when the sandbox is deleted.
- A 404 means the sandbox has already been deleted.

### Errors

Every error is JSON with a `message`. A 422 adds `errors`, one entry per field to fix:

```json
{
  "message": "Unprocessable Entity: validation failed.",
  "errors": [{"path": "project.version", "message": "There is no release of pathauto with the version 8.x-99.0."}]
}
```

- 400: the body is not a JSON object.
- 422: the body breaks a rule. Fix the fields in `errors` and send it again.
- 429: too many launches or lookups from this IP address. Wait the number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header.
- 503: the sandbox host failed to start the sandbox. Try again in a few minutes.
